title: Rightward cleanup run
statement: Let $M$ be a $k$-work-tape Turing machine, let $q_0$ be an initial state, and fix an input, an index $i<k$, an input-head position, output word, and integer bound $B$. Let $a,b$ be integers, and let $D_t,M_t$ be tape contents and $D_p,M_p$ be head positions for the two banks of work tapes. Suppose $M_t(i)$ is the tape marking the origin and the interval from $a$ through $b$, $0\le b$, and $b+1\le B$. For every $n$ and head-position function $D_p$ such that $b+1-D_p(i)=n$, $a\le D_p(i)$, and $|D_p(j)|\le B$ for every tape index $j$, the cleanup machine started in its rightward-walk phase at index $i$ has all work-head positions bounded in absolute value by $B$ at every time $t\le n+1$. At time $n+1$ it is in the erasing phase at index $i$, with both banks' head positions updated at $i$ to $b$ and all other configuration data unchanged.
hypotheses_covered: A fixed Boolean input, input-head position, output word, and bound $B$.
Integer endpoints $a,b$, tape contents $D_t,M_t$, and head positions $D_p,M_p$.
The second-bank tape at $i$ is marked on the origin and the interval from $a$ to $b$.
